text:
maria: Heads-up — planning a config-only rollout in 5m for tiny-safeguard changes. No model binary updates.

Changes: 1) batching_window_ms: 80 -> 30; 2) route_weight_floor: 0.02 -> 0.05 for background tier; 3) request_timeout_s: 6 -> 5; 4) small increase to per-tenant qps_shaper for warmup.

maria: Canary at 5% traffic, 10m observation, then 25% if green. Deploybot will gate.

ash: ack. adding to preflight checklist — observability flips: 99p latency, p50, error-rate by tenant, and kvcache hit rate. I’ll standby for metrics.

deploy-bot: deploy started by maria (config-only).
```
canary_percent=5
deploy_type=config-only
changes=[batching_window_ms:80->30, route_weight_floor:0.02->0.05, timeout_s:6->5]
canary_duration=10m
```

jordan: quick question — the route_floor bump could kick some background tenants to the dedicated path sooner; did we test the fallback?

maria: yes — we ran local sim with synthetic traffic. Fallback policy remains: if latency > 1200ms or error rate spike > 1%, route falls back to old weights. I added a canary-only kill-switch.

sam: FYI I reduced the soft-concurrency on the batcher to avoid small bursts causing queueing. That should keep p99 steady. config diff pasted in #infra-prs.

ash: deploy-bot reports: canary active at 5% (started). Watching dashboards — numbers in ~2m.

deploy-bot: metrics snapshot (canary-start): p50=110ms, p99=680ms, errors=0.12%, kvcache_hit=72%

jordan: those look fine. keep an eye on tail — if p99 crosses 900ms for 2 consecutive minutes we abort.

maria: agreed. If we see kvcache_hit drop >8% that’s a sign of cold-cache regressions and we should roll back.

ash: +1. I’ll keep a script ready to pin routing to previous weights: `./infra/pin-route --tenant=all --to=prev`

deploy-bot: canary 5% -> metrics at 5m: p50=115ms, p99=720ms, errors=0.18%, kvcache_hit=69%

sam: small uptick on errors for one background tenant (tenant-42) — looking. Might be traffic shape.

maria: ok holding at 5% for now. Jordan, can you run a quick replay of tenant-42 workload locally?

jordan: on it. Replay looks like increased transient queueing when batching window tightens for long inputs. I’ll try bumping the per-tenant qps_shaper for tenant-42 and re-run.

maria: go ahead. If fix is quick we can continue ramp. If not, we rollback and re-evaluate the batching_window delta.

deploy-bot: canary 5% -> 9m metrics: p50=118ms, p99=760ms, errors=0.25%, kvcache_hit=67%

ash: errors trending up but still below abort threshold. But p99 creeping. Recommend holding and not progressing to 25% yet.

maria: hold recognized. I’m toggling the canary kill-switch to prevent auto-ramp.

deploy-bot: auto-ramp disabled. Manual control only.

sam: after increasing tenant-42 shaper to 1.2x, replay p99 drops ~150ms locally. Might be okay. We should patch tenant-specific shaper as a targeted mitigation rather than full rollback.

jordan: concur. I'll open a short-lived override: route_weight_floor stays, but tenant-42 gets `qps_shaper:1.2x` via runtime flag.

maria: please do that and we’ll watch for 3m. If stable, continue canary to 25% with another 10m watch.

jordan: override applied.

deploy-bot: runtime flag applied to tenant-42.

deploy-bot: metrics 3m after override: p50=112ms, p99=640ms, errors=0.14%, kvcache_hit=71%

ash: nice. Safe to advance?

maria: yes. Moving to 25% now. Remember no code change — easier rollback if needed.

deploy-bot: ramping to 25% over 60s.

deploy-bot: metrics (during ramp): p99 stabilized ~700ms, errors steady 0.15%.

sam: I’ll add a note in release notes: config-only — batching_window->30ms, route_floor->0.05, timeout->5s, tenant-42 shaper override applied temporarily.

maria: thx. After the 10m observation we’ll unpin the override if stable and promote to full. If anything regresses we rollback the config-only change and revert the shaper override.
